items.example: We were pretty hard up when I was a kid.
items.exampleTr: Ben çocukken epey darda kalmıştık.
items.simple: Not having enough money, often for a long time.
dialogue: A: Why don't you ask your parents for help?
B: They're pretty hard up themselves.
items.note: 'skint'ten daha uzun süreli yoksulluk; biraz eski usul ama yaygın.

items.example: I'm feeling flush this month, dinner's on me.
items.exampleTr: Bu ay cebim dolu, yemek benden.
items.simple: Having lots of money right now, for a short time.
dialogue: A: You bought everyone drinks?
B: I just got my bonus, so I'm flush.
items.note: Gayriresmî; genelde maaş ya da ikramiyeden sonra.

items.tr: (bir şeye) har vurup harman savurmak, çılgınca para harcamak
items.example: I splurged on a really nice coat in the sales.
items.exampleTr: İndirimde çok güzel bir montu kafaya taktım ve aldım.
items.simple: Spend a lot of money on something nice, just for fun.
dialogue: A: Nice watch!
B: Thanks. I decided to splurge for my birthday.
items.note: Fiil ve isim: 'a little splurge' = küçük bir şımarıklık.

items.example: I'm already deep into my overdraft and it's only the tenth.
items.exampleTr: Ayın daha onu ve şimdiden eksi hesaba epey girdim.
items.simple: Money the bank lets you spend when your account is empty.
dialogue: A: Can you lend me fifty quid?
B: Sorry, I'm in my overdraft myself.
items.note: 'go into my overdraft' = hesabı eksiye düşürmek.

items.example: You have to haggle at the market, nobody pays full price.
items.exampleTr: Pazarda pazarlık etmen lazım, kimse tam fiyat ödemez.
items.simple: Talk with a seller to make the price lower.
dialogue: A: He wanted forty for that lamp.
B: Did you haggle? I'd have paid twenty.
items.note: 'haggle over the price' kalıbı.

items.example: The landlord just hit us with a massive rent hike.
items.exampleTr: Ev sahibi bize kocaman bir kira artışı yaptı.
items.simple: When the owner suddenly makes you pay more money to live there.
dialogue: A: Why are you moving out?
B: We just got a rent hike, and I can't afford it.
items.note: 'hike' = ani ve büyük artış; 'price hike' da yaygın.

items.example: I came back from the conference with a bag full of freebies.
items.exampleTr: Konferanstan bir çanta dolusu promosyonla döndüm.
items.simple: A small thing you get for free, like a pen or a sample.
dialogue: A: Where did you get that mug?
B: It was a freebie from the bank.
items.note: Gayriresmî; fuar, otel, mağaza için.

items.example: The taxi driver totally fleeced us.
items.exampleTr: Taksici bizi fena kazıkladı.
items.simple: Take too much money from someone by tricking them.
dialogue: A: Twelve euros for a coffee?
B: They fleece tourists here.
items.note: Gayriresmî; turist tuzakları için çok yaygın.

items.example: We've built up a nice little nest egg for retirement.
items.exampleTr: Emeklilik için kenarda güzel bir birikim yaptık.
items.simple: Money you save slowly and keep safe for later.
dialogue: A: Are you going to spend the inheritance?
B: No, it'll be a nest egg for the kids.
items.note: 'a nice little nest egg' çok tipik.

items.example: I had to dip into my savings to fix the car.
items.exampleTr: Arabayı tamir ettirmek için birikimime el atmak zorunda kaldım.
items.simple: Take some of the money you saved, because you need it now.
dialogue: A: How did you pay for the new boiler?
B: I had to dip into my savings.
items.note: 'my' kişiye göre değişir.

items.example: I cleaned the whole flat so I'd get my deposit back.
items.exampleTr: Depozitomu geri alayım diye bütün daireyi temizledim.
items.simple: Get back the money you paid the owner before you moved in.
dialogue: A: Why are you scrubbing the oven?
B: I want to get my deposit back.
items.note: Kiracılıkta: 'The landlord kept my deposit' = depozitomu vermedi.

items.example: Just set up a direct debit and you'll never miss a bill.
items.exampleTr: Otomatik ödeme talimatı ver, hiçbir faturayı kaçırmazsın.
items.simple: Tell the bank to pay a bill by itself every month.
dialogue: A: I keep forgetting to pay the gym.
B: Why don't you set up a direct debit?
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; ABD'de 'set up autopay'.

items.example: It's eight hundred a month, bills included.
items.exampleTr: Aylığı sekiz yüz, faturalar dahil.
items.simple: The price already has water, power and internet in it.
dialogue: A: Is the rent for the flat high?
B: Not really. It's six hundred, bills included.
items.note: Kiralık ilanlarında çok sık; 'excluding bills' = faturalar hariç.

items.example: We're a bit strapped for cash until the end of the month.
items.exampleTr: Ay sonuna kadar biraz eli darız.
items.simple: Not having enough money right now.
dialogue: A: Want to come to the gig?
B: I'm a bit strapped for cash this week.
items.note: Gayriresmî ama kibar; 'skint' kadar argo değil.

items.tr: maaştan maaşa, ancak ay sonunu getirerek
items.example: Most of my friends are living paycheck to paycheck.
items.exampleTr: Arkadaşlarımın çoğu maaştan maaşa yaşıyor.
items.simple: All your money is gone before you get paid again.
dialogue: A: Have you got any savings?
B: Savings? I live paycheck to paycheck.
items.note: ABD kökenli; İngiltere'de 'payday to payday' de denir.

items.example: Eight pounds for a pint? That's daylight robbery!
items.exampleTr: Bir bira sekiz pound mu? Bu düpedüz soygun!
items.simple: A price that is so high it feels like stealing.
dialogue: A: Parking here is twenty quid a day.
B: Daylight robbery!
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; ABD'de 'highway robbery'.

items.example: Always read the small print before you sign.
items.exampleTr: İmzalamadan önce küçük puntolu şartları mutlaka oku.
items.simple: The tiny writing in a contract, where the bad news hides.
dialogue: A: The phone deal was free, but now they want money.
B: Did you read the small print?
items.note: ABD'de 'the fine print'.

items.example: There's so much red tape just to get a parking permit.
items.exampleTr: Sadece park izni almak için bile o kadar bürokrasi var ki.
items.simple: Lots of forms and slow rules that make simple things take ages.
dialogue: A: Have you got your visa yet?
B: No, I'm still stuck in red tape.
items.note: 'cut through the red tape' = bürokrasiyi aşmak.

items.example: If you book last minute, you pay through the nose.
items.exampleTr: Son dakika alırsan kazığı yersin.
items.simple: Pay much more money than something should cost.
dialogue: A: How much were the concert tickets?
B: Don't ask. We had to pay through the nose.
items.note: 'pay through the nose for something' kalıbı.

items.example: With the baby coming, we'll have to tighten our belts.
items.exampleTr: Bebek geliyor, kemerleri sıkmamız gerekecek.
items.simple: Spend less money because times are hard.
dialogue: A: No holiday this year?
B: Nope. We need to tighten our belts.
items.note: 'our' kişiye göre değişir; Türkçedeki 'kemer sıkmak' ile birebir.

items.example: That old house turned out to be a money pit.
items.exampleTr: O eski ev tam bir para kuyusu çıktı.
items.simple: A thing that keeps needing more and more money, like an old house.
dialogue: A: Another repair on the car?
B: I know. It's a money pit.
items.note: Ev, eski araba, tekne için.

items.example: Let's go halves on a taxi.
items.exampleTr: Taksiyi yarı yarıya ödeyelim.
items.simple: Two people each pay half.
dialogue: A: That pizza's huge.
B: Want to go halves?
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi, gayriresmî; 'go halves on something'.

items.example: I've been stuck on hold with the bank for forty minutes.
items.exampleTr: Kırk dakikadır bankada telefonda bekletiliyorum.
items.simple: Waiting on the phone, listening to music, for someone to answer.
dialogue: A: Did you sort out the internet bill?
B: No, I was stuck on hold for an hour.
items.note: 'put someone on hold' = hatta bekletmek.

items.example: Money's a bit tight at the moment, so we're staying in.
items.exampleTr: Şu an paralar biraz kısıtlı, o yüzden evdeyiz.
items.simple: There isn't much money right now.
dialogue: A: Are you coming skiing this year?
B: I'd love to, but money's a bit tight.
items.note: Para sıkıntısını kibarca söylemenin en yaygın yolu.

items.example: What's the going rate for a babysitter these days?
items.exampleTr: Bu aralar bebek bakıcısının piyasa ücreti ne kadar?
items.simple: The normal price most people pay for something right now.
dialogue: A: He wants fifteen an hour for tutoring.
B: That's about the going rate.
items.note: Ücret, kira, hizmet bedeli sorarken.

items.tr: kâr da zarar da etmemek, başa baş gelmek
items.example: After all the costs, we barely managed to break even.
items.exampleTr: Tüm masraflardan sonra ancak başa baş geldik.
items.simple: You make back the same money you spent, no more, no less.
dialogue: A: Did the bake sale make any money?
B: We just about managed to break even.
items.note: Yan iş, etkinlik, garaj satışı için de.
